name: Amanda Walker
life: “I still remember cake served on a plate borrowed from our neighbors.” Friday often includes a stop at Breakwater Way, where Amanda stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I was the child eating the cake. I want to pay for the next family whose grown-ups whisper at the till.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a charcoal zip cardigan and one cuff folded back twice. Amanda has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, with a high puff tied with plain cord. Amanda squares up pieces of paper while thinking during a conversation.
personality: Amanda carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To fund a meal for another bereaved family.
family: Martha Ueda is Amanda’s half-sibling. Amanda can always ask for five minutes alone. Martha asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *Care with a clock*, Martha says, “I have been buying an extra fifteen minutes for my father without telling my sister I'm in debt.”
connections: Devin Mills (parent). Parent and grown child decide what the belated payment can do for another bereaved household.

reactions.situation: The shop owners disagree on what to do with the payment
reactions.response: Amanda asks both owners for figures before anyone promises a fund or a repair.

reactions.situation: A stranger waves a phone camera in a crying person's face
reactions.response: Amanda offers an ordinary errand that lets the distressed person leave without being followed by an audience.
